parts.text: A student investigates the cooling of water in a metal container.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) The student uses a thermometer to measure room temperature θ R . Room temperature is 23 °C. Show clearly, on Fig. 2.1, the reading θ R . [1]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Fig. 2.2 shows the apparatus set up for the investigation. The student pours 200 cm 3 of hot water into the metal container. She places the thermometer in the hot water in the container. She records the temperature at time t = 0. She immediately starts a stop-watch. She records the temperature in Table 2.1 at 30 s intervals until she has seven sets of readings. Complete the column headings in Table 2.1. [1] Table 2.1 t / θ / 0 92 0.5 86 1.0 82 1.5 79 2.0 77 2.5 75 3.0 74

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Plot a graph of temperature θ (y-axis) against time t (x-axis). Label your axes appropriately. You do not need to start the y-axis at 0. Draw the best-fit curve. [4]

ms.label: 2(c)
ms.text:
Graph:
Axes correctly labelled and right way round
Suitable scales
All plots correct to ½ small square
Good line judgement, thin, continuous line

ms.label: 2(d)
ms.text:
Statement to match graph line
Explanation to match statement and line.

parts.label: f
parts.text: (f) Draw a measuring cylinder containing water. On your diagram show the line of sight you use to obtain an accurate reading of the volume of water. [2]

ms.label: 2(f)
ms.text:
Measuring cylinder drawn with liquid
Clear indication of line of sight at right angles to cylinder and level with surface of liquid.
